material: Detail 1: 4130 or 8630 steel. Detail 4: 4140, RC 34–39, four required. Detail 5: 4140 HT, RC 34–39, one required.
finish: Detail 1: carburize and harden .030–.040 deep; wear surfaces RC 58–62 and grind; all other surfaces RC 40–45; temper at 350–400 °F after quench. Break all sharp corners and remove burrs. warnings: Sheet 2 of 2, dated March 1, 1979, model 220 B. Includes detail 1 plus separate details 4 and 5. Do not fuse separate components. Detail 4 requires four pieces; detail 5 one.
Tool-number suffix is faint; best reading SB-12054-1. Stamped marking explicitly reads SB-12054. Confirm title-block suffix before release.
No governing ASME/ANSI/ISO/DIN designation is printed. Inch units and third-angle projection are explicit.
Front keyway width and radial extent are readable, but full axial termination is not safely established. Resolve before completing model.
Rear-slot R. TYP. and detail-4 end R. lack printed numerical magnitudes. D050/D054 are conditional semicircle inferences requiring confirmation.

H005 DIAMETER .250 IS NOMINAL SCREW SIZE ONLY, NOT A SPECIFIED HOLE DIAMETER. Schema requires a positive diameter, so the screw-size value is retained as a clearly flagged placeholder. Actual clearance-hole diameter, counterbore diameter and counterbore depth are unknown. Block F026 from automated building until resolved. Zero counterbore fields mean unknown, not absent.
H005 quantity four is one hole in each of four separate detail-4 components, not a four-hole pattern in one part. Assembly positions are absent, so instance_positions are empty.
Tapped-hole diameters are nominal thread sizes, not tap-drill diameters. Thread classes, explicit series, pilot sizes and blind drill-point allowances are unspecified.
Radial .500-13 TAP THRU passes through one wall into bore at axial station 2.00. Confirm angular clocking from aligned section trace; do not drill both opposite walls.
Six mounting-hole coordinates are nominally hexagonal but rounded: preserve 2.923 and 1.687 with ±.005 rather than forcing exact trigonometric coordinates. Ø6.750 bolt circle is REF.
Main hole instance positions reference lower-left corner of the 8-inch circular envelope. Rear-hole positions use rear-view orientation. Detail-5 positions use its separate .936-inch envelope.
Angular dimension values and angular spacing are degrees. The schema has no degree unit, so angular dimensions retain inch only as the drawing-unit metadata.
Gauge balls are inspection aids, not chuck components. The 4.195 between-balls measurement is not a bore diameter.
The .38 radius leader points to front flange root and is not marked TYP.; confirm whether it also controls the drawn rounded rear transition.
The .030 bore-step radius is nearly the .031 radial step height between Ø4.500 and Ø4.562; do not enlarge it for visual convenience.
No general four-decimal tolerance is supplied for the .5000 gauge-ball diameter. Geometric .0005 values are explicit controls, not ± dimensional tolerances.
Runout frames show a single-arrow symbol with TIR wording; transcribed as circular runout, not automatically total runout.
General tolerances follow printed decimal places; they do not define thread fits, unspecified radii, gauge accuracy or tolerances on derived dimensions.
